vectors.description: control: a canonical RFC 8032 signature is accepted by BOTH strict (libsodium) and ZIP215 verification

ZIP215-ONLY signature: R is the identity point in its NON-CANONICAL encoding (y = p+1), S = k*a mod L. Satisfies the cofactored equation [8]S*B = [8]R + [8]k*A (accepted by a ZIP215 verifier such as noble zip215:true); STRICT RFC 8032 rejects it (non-canonical R encoding; libsodium also rejects small-order R). Every r402s component pins zip215:false and MUST reject

RFC 9180 Appendix A.2.1 (Base mode; DHKEM(X25519,HKDF-SHA256) 0x0020, HKDF-SHA256 0x0001, ChaCha20-Poly1305 0x0003 = the r402s-1 suite): DeriveKeyPair(ikmE)/(ikmR) and enc, byte-equal. The generator proved these under pyhpke before emitting any vector; @hpke/core and rust-hpke must reproduce them (D182 acceptance 1)
vectors.notes: shared_secret/key_schedule_context/secret/key/base_nonce/exporter_secret are the RFC's internal values, reproduced verbatim for implementations that expose them; the public single-shot API only exposes enc/ct/export, which is what the verifier checks

vectors.description: RFC 9180 A.2.1.1 encryptions: the SAME sender context sealing sequence numbers 0..256 with aad="Count-<n>"; ct at 0,1,2,4,255,256 byte-equal (nonce = base_nonce XOR seq)
RFC 9180 A.2.1.2 exported values (exporter_context empty / 0x00 / "TestContext", L=32)

key_envelope SEAL/OPEN round-trip: ct = HPKE-Base seal of the raw 32-byte K_repo (48 bytes); enc = the 32-byte ephemeral X25519 pubkey; info = lp("r402s/v0/envelope")||lp(suite)||lp(SHA-256(recipient raw pubkey) hex)||lp(created_by); AAD = JCS({repo_id,epoch,recipient_kind,recipient_fingerprint}); signed under domain key_envelope; the genesis receipt = {object_kind,epoch,recipient_fingerprint,stored_bytes_sha256,size_bytes} of these stored bytes. Deterministic: the ephemeral keypair = DeriveKeyPair(ikmE)
TAMPER: ct byte 0 flipped -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: ct tag byte (last) flipped -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: enc byte 0 flipped (a different KEM encapsulation) -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: WRONG RECIPIENT: opened with a different X25519 private key -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: AAD field `repo_id` changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: AAD field `epoch` changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: AAD field `recipient_kind` changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: AAD field `recipient_fingerprint` changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: info element 0 (label) changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: info element 1 (suite) changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: info element 2 (recipient pubkey SHA-256) changed to another key's digest -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)
TAMPER: info element 3 (sender signing fingerprint) changed -> open fails (the recipient recovers no key)

SIGNATURE-BEFORE-OPEN: a key_envelope whose bytes changed after signing (created_at) fails signature verification; the recipient MUST NOT attempt the HPKE open (the ct/enc inside would still open — that is exactly why the order matters)
exact-scalar reject: a 63-char ct (47 bytes) is a SCHEMA reject before any cryptography (ct = exactly 64 base64url chars = 48 bytes = 32 + 16 tag)

recovery_receipt (creator-signed, domain recovery_receipt): genesis_sha256 = the genesis stored-bytes hash of stored-001; both fingerprints equal the genesis key bindings (semantic constraint genesis-key-bindings)

RECEIPT-LED RECOVERY round-trip: receipt pin -> genesis (hash equal; signature valid) -> its envelope receipt -> the stored key_envelope (hash equal; signature valid; path identity (epoch, recipient_fingerprint) equal) -> HPKE open with the creator's encryption key -> K_repo -> k_obj(wal_pack) -> the aead-001 WAL frame decrypts to the known plaintext

a recovery_receipt whose genesis_sha256 names other bytes (here head 1) does NOT pin this genesis: the recovery is refused as unauthenticated salvage (the receipt is correctly signed and schema-valid — the pin is what fails)
a recovery_receipt whose creator_encryption_fingerprint differs from the genesis envelope recipient -> genesis-key-bindings violated (the receipt's fingerprints MUST equal the genesis pair)
FOREIGN ENVELOPE FINGERPRINT: genesis whose envelopes[0].recipient_fingerprint != ek_fingerprint(creator_encryption_pubkey) — schema-valid and correctly signed, never canonizes (genesis-key-bindings)
UNRELATED writer_key_id: genesis signed by the creator but naming a writer_key_id != vk_fingerprint(creator_signing_pubkey) (genesis-key-bindings)
ENVELOPE RECEIPT HASH MISMATCH: the genesis receipt's stored_bytes_sha256 is not the hash of the stored key_envelope bytes (envelope-receipt-binding)

STORED ENVELOPE created_by != genesis writer_key_id: a correctly signed envelope naming another creator does not bind to this genesis (genesis-key-bindings: the stored envelope's repo_id/epoch/recipient_fingerprint/created_by equal the genesis values). Note the HPKE open also fails: created_by is an info element
envelope receipt epoch != 0000000000000001 is a SCHEMA reject (genesis epoch is a const and the receipt's epoch is pinned to it)
FIRST PAGE: GET …/heads?after_generation=2&limit=2 with NO cursor -> generations 3,4 under `heads`, the anchor echoed, has_more true with an opaque next_cursor, total null (not yet known)
CONTINUATION: the prior page's next_cursor echoed UNCHANGED as `cursor`, SAME after_generation -> generations 5,6; the sequence is gapless across the page boundary
FINAL PAGE: continuation of page 2 -> generation 7, has_more false, next_cursor null, total "5" = exactly the generations delivered above the anchor across the whole sequence
MISSING after_generation: the anchor is REQUIRED (a semantic verification input, not a paging knob) — the request is refused by the request schema before any listing
MALFORMED cursor ("not a cursor!" violates the opaque-token grammar) -> INVALID_CURSOR, never a silent restart from the pin
STALE cursor — minted for ANOTHER VAULT under the same anchor: well-formed, schema-valid, but not bound to this vault -> INVALID_CURSOR
vectors.notes: schema-valid-but-protocol-invalid: the request validates; the refusal comes from the cursor's vault binding

vectors.description: ANCHOR DRIFT: page 1's cursor (minted under after_generation=2) presented with after_generation=3 — after_generation must stay CONSTANT across a page sequence; a continuation that changes its anchor is not a continuation -> INVALID_CURSOR
TAMPERED cursor: page 1's next_cursor with its last character altered — still grammatical, but not a token the platform minted (store and echo, never parse or edit) -> INVALID_CURSOR
COUPLING (a) has_more false + next_cursor null: the final-page shape — ACCEPT
COUPLING (b) has_more true + opaque next_cursor: the continuation shape — ACCEPT
COUPLING (c) has_more false + a non-null next_cursor: contradictory — schema REJECT (the if/then/else coupling)
COUPLING (d) has_more true + next_cursor null: a page that claims more but offers no continuation — schema REJECT

RETIRED MEMBER: the retired continuation field `next_after_generation` on an otherwise valid final page — rejected by additionalProperties: false (an SDK generated from the old schema would expect it; the frozen contract forbids it)

EMPTY INTERMEDIATE PAGE: heads [] with has_more true + next_cursor is a legal shape (a scan window that held no listing keys; the continuation must still make progress) — total null because it is not yet known

EMPTY FINAL PAGE with a truthful total: limit=5 delivered 3..7 as a FULL page that is never silently the end (has_more true); the continuation returns heads [], has_more false, next_cursor null, total "5"
UNTRUTHFUL total: the final page says total "4" while the sequence delivered 5 generations above the anchor — total is exact or null, never a nearby number -> REJECT
CROSS-PAGE GAP: page 1 ended at 4, the continuation starts at 6 — generations are gapless within AND across pages; a gap fails closed as CHAIN_BROKEN (§6.3)
limit above MAX_HEADS_PER_LISTING_PAGE (1001) is refused by the request schema
A page entry AT the anchor (generation 2 with after_generation=2): every listed generation is strictly above the pin -> REJECT

MISSING limit: D186 makes `limit` REQUIRED — a missing or malformed limit is a request-validation refusal (an SDK generated from a schema where limit is optional would disagree with the server before page one) -> refused by the request schema

FORWARD GUARD TRUE: the stored cut bytes at the per-attempt key hash to p_cut_sha256 -> the ONLY enabled live transition is record_put_issued_p_credit; admission -> RECORD_PUT_ISSUED; nothing else changes (D155/D158 mechanical progression)

FORWARD GUARD FALSE (one stored byte flipped): an EXTERNAL storage-integrity fault, not an admission outcome (D190) -> CUT_STORAGE_INTEGRITY_FAILURE; NO record PUT; the ONLY changed coordinate is the storage_integrity marker — admission, lane, claims, stage reservation, cut ownership (the attempt key stays burned), replacement, rate slot, lease, authority time all unchanged; not ABORTED, not CONFLICTED, not DR_ORPHANED_PRE_RECORD
FORWARD GUARD FALSE (the stored object ABSENT at the per-attempt key): the same storage-integrity fault — the guard requires the bytes to EXIST and hash to p_cut_sha256

FAIL-CLOSED: the faulted attempt with the bytes STILL wrong enables NO live transition (no record PUT, no abort, no release — the client cannot retry its way out; restore or an operator recovery decision is the only exit)
RESTORATION: the exact journaled cut bytes restored at the SAME burned per-attempt key -> cut_integrity_restored lifts the marker (the only changed coordinate); the attempt id / key are unchanged
AFTER RESTORATION the forward guard holds and the mechanical path resumes: record_put_issued_p_credit -> RECORD_PUT_ISSUED (the attempt continues, it is never re-admitted)

SUCCESSOR C1 with the replacement PENDING: the storage-integrity fault leaves the replacement arm PENDING and the predecessor the sole open cycle (no clear, no install, no terminal) — a fault is not an adjudication
